title: MCP server discoverable
question: Can an agent find an MCP server for this site through a documented route?
method: Look for a server card through the routes the MCP Server Card extension and the AI Catalog proposal describe, in this order and within six requests: up to two entries of type application/mcp-server-card+json in /.well-known/ai-catalog.json (inline or by URL), then a card at <endpoint>/server-card for up to two endpoints hinted on the site's own host (a Link header with rel=mcp-server on the home page, or an llms.txt link whose path contains mcp), then the community paths /.well-known/mcp/server-card (the path the extension's discovery document names) and the older /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json. A card counts when it parses with a name and an http(s) endpoint URL. Pass on a card from the AI Catalog or an endpoint hint. Warn when only a community path answers (neither is in the specification), saying which. Fail when a card URL answers 200 with something that is not a card with a name and an endpoint. Skipped as not applicable when no card is found, because the file is optional. When a card URL is refused or challenged (401, 402, 403, 406, 429, 451 or a bot-management challenge) or fails transiently, the check is skipped as inconclusive and names the refusal rather than reporting a missing card. Server Cards are an official MCP extension at Beta stage, but no host documents probing these files yet (agents are given MCP URLs by hand or through registries), hence the low weight.

title: API catalog
question: Does the site publish an API catalog linkset?
method: GET /.well-known/api-catalog. Pass on 200 with a JSON document that carries a linkset array with at least one link, whatever the content type (application/linkset+json is expected, and another type is noted). Skipped as not applicable on 404 or 410, because the file is optional. Fail on any other status, on an HTML page (a soft 404 or a challenge), on a body without a linkset array, and on a linkset that lists no links. Skipped when the request was rate limited or failed (429, a gateway error or no response). No answer engine documents reading it: a convention.

title: OAuth discovery for the MCP endpoint
question: Can an agent discover how to authorize against the MCP server?
method: For the MCP endpoint found by A4.1, on the endpoint's origin, GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/<endpoint path> and then /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (RFC 9728, which the MCP specification requires of authorized servers). If neither carries metadata, GET the endpoint and read its WWW-Authenticate header. If that does not help, GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (RFC 8414). Pass when protected resource metadata with a non-empty authorization_servers list is found, or when the endpoint answers 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header naming resource_metadata. Warn when only authorization server metadata (an issuer with an authorization or token endpoint) exists. Fail when the endpoint answers 401 and none of them exists, so an agent cannot find where to sign in. Skipped as not applicable when the endpoint does not answer 401: the MCP specification makes authorization optional, so an open endpoint needs no OAuth discovery. Skipped when A4.1 found no endpoint.

title: MCP endpoint reachable
question: Does the advertised MCP endpoint answer like an MCP server?
method: POST a JSON-RPC server/discover request (the read-only method the 2026-07-28 specification makes mandatory) to the endpoint from the server card, with the 2026-07-28 headers. Pass when the answer is a JSON-RPC message, whatever the status: a result, or the errors the Streamable HTTP transport prescribes (404 with -32601 from an older server that does not implement server/discover, 400 with -32020 on a header mismatch). An event stream also passes, and so does a 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header (a server that requires authorization). When server/discover gets a plain HTTP 400 without a JSON-RPC body, as a server on the 2025 session transport answers anything before a session exists, send the 2025-06-18 initialize handshake once and pass when it answers with a JSON-RPC message. Fail on a 404 or any other answer without a JSON-RPC body, such as a 401 without WWW-Authenticate, a 405, a 500 or an HTML page. Skipped when the request is rate limited (429), meets a gateway error (502, 503, 504) or gets no response, and when A4.1 found no endpoint. These are the only requests the scanner sends with a body. They create nothing on the server beyond the session the handshake opens.

title: A2A agent card
question: Does the site publish a valid A2A agent card?
method: GET /.well-known/agent-card.json. Pass on a JSON object with the eight fields A2A 1.0 requires: name, description, supportedInterfaces, version, capabilities, defaultInputModes, defaultOutputModes and skills. Warn when the card lacks some of them, naming the missing ones. Fail when that URL answers 200 with something that is not a JSON object. When it does not answer 200, try the pre-0.3 path /.well-known/agent.json and warn when an A2A card is found only there. JSON at that path counts as an A2A card only when it carries name, description, url or supportedInterfaces, version, capabilities and skills, because other agent-discovery drafts use the same path. Skipped as not applicable when no card is found at either path, because the file is optional, and as inconclusive when a request was rate limited or failed. No shopping agent documents reading agent cards from stores: a convention.

title: WebMCP tool declarations
question: Does the site declare in-page tools for browser agents?
method: Informational. On the home page and the sampled product pages, look for forms that declare a WebMCP tool (toolname and tooldescription, with toolparamdescription on fields) and for document.modelContext or navigator.modelContext in inline scripts. Pass when found. Warn when a form carries toolname without tooldescription (the browser does not register it) or when a page that declares tools sends Permissions-Policy: tools=(), which turns WebMCP off. Not applicable when the HTML declares none. Tools registered from bundled scripts are invisible to a scan that does not run JavaScript. The API is a W3C community draft in origin trials in Chrome and Edge with one shipping consumer (ChatGPT's site tools in its desktop browser). No shopping agent documents calling it on arbitrary stores, so this is reported and never scored.

spec.title: WebMCP (W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group draft)

title: WordPress REST API readable
question: Can an agent read the WordPress site's content through its REST API without signing in?
method: Runs only on WordPress sites (WooCommerce included). Take the REST API root the page advertises with the api.w.org link relation (in the head, else the Link header, if it is on the same origin), else /wp-json/, and GET wp/v2/pages?per_page=1&_fields=id,link without signing in. Pass on 200 with a JSON array, even an empty one. Fail on 401 or 403 (a security plugin or filter refuses anonymous reads, typically with rest_not_logged_in), on 404, and on any other answer that is not a JSON array. Warn when robots.txt keeps the scanner from asking. Skipped on 429, a gateway error or no response. WordPress advises against disabling the API, and the WooCommerce Store API runs on it.

spec.title: WordPress REST API Handbook: Frequently asked questions

title: Wix site MCP server answers
question: Does the MCP server Wix runs for every site answer agents?
method: Runs only on Wix sites. Send the read-only JSON-RPC server/discover POST to /_api/mcp, where Wix documents an MCP server for every site that needs no authentication and that the generated llms.txt links. When it gets a plain HTTP 400, as a server on the 2025 session transport answers, send the initialize handshake once instead. Pass on a JSON-RPC answer, an event stream or an authorization challenge (401 with WWW-Authenticate). Fail on any other answer, such as a 404, an HTML page or a server error. Warn when robots.txt keeps the scanner from asking. Skipped when the request gets no response, a rate limit (HTTP 429) or a gateway error (502, 503 or 504).

spec.title: Wix Developers: About the Wix site MCP

title: Shopware agentic files
question: Has the Shopware sales channel published its agentic files?
method: Runs only on Shopware stores. GET /.well-known/ai-catalog.json, one of the three agentic files (with /llms.txt and /agents.md) that Shopware 6.7.12 and later publishes when they are switched on for the sales channel. Pass on 200 with a JSON object. Warn on 404 (the file is off, or the shop runs an older version), on any other answer that is not a JSON object, and when robots.txt keeps the scanner from asking. Skipped on 429, a gateway error or no response.
